text:
anna: Hey team, incoming escalation from a customer (high-priority). They saw p99 jump from ~900ms -> ~6.2s starting ~01:15 UTC. They reported a bunch of 503s and a lot of long tails. Attaching logs they sent: 

anna: ```
2026-02-12T01:16:02Z ERROR attach failed request_id=req_9f2a timeout=45s err=capacity_unavailable
2026-02-12T01:16:03Z WARN response delay request_id=req_9f3b p95=2.1s p99=6.4s
2026-02-12T01:18:10Z ERROR attach failed request_id=req_9f5c code=503 msg="no capacity"
```

anna: Customer says they were on a Dedicated pool (dedicated-eu1) and hit this during steady traffic — not a single big burst. They opened a support ticket with request ids above. Can SRE/oncall triage? :warning:

jamie: oncall here. I'm booting up dashboards. Which tenant/org?

anna: Tenant id: t-acme-42. They were using model=rwd-2 (quantized) pinned to v1. No recent rollout per their note.

deploy-bot: deploy finished: services/dedicated-provisioner @ commit abc123 (2026-02-12T00:48:09Z)

kevin: Looking at provisioning metrics now. Quick Prom query I ran: 

kevin: ```promql
sum(rate(dedicated_pool_attach_failures_total{pool="dedicated-eu1"}[5m])) by (reason)
```

kevin: Over 01:10-01:30 UTC I see attach_failures spike (reason="cold_start") and queue_depth for pool jumped to ~120 pending, attach_rate flattened. p99 spike aligns with pending > 100.

maria: That sounds like a scale-up lag + cold GPU warmup issue. Any image pull/errors? Kernel image pulls can add 30-90s to warmup if nodes are being provisioned fresh.

kevin: Logs show a lot of node bootstrap timeouts and kubelet backoff on a subset of hosts: 

kevin: ```
Feb 12 01:12:38 node-370 kubelet[...]: Error pulling image "rwd-runtime:v5": context deadline exceeded
Feb 12 01:13:05 node-370 systemd[1]: start request repeated too quickly for rwd-runtime.service
```

jamie: So probable root cause: dedicated-eu1 exhausted warm nodes, autoscaler requested new nodes, but new nodes struggled with image pulls -> attach queue backed up -> p99 spike + 503s.

anna: Customer wants an ETA and mitigation steps ASAP. They said traffic is steady, not a one-off spike.

maria: Short-term mitigations we can propose to customer: 
- Enable tenant burst capacity (allow fallback to shared-hosted for small percentage of requests) 
- Increase prewarm pool size for model=rwd-2 on dedicated-eu1 
- Temporarily relax pin (redirect to rwd-2-fallback)

maria: For internal immediate mitigation: incrementally bump pool.desired_replicas for dedicated-eu1 by +6 to drain queue, and roll out alternate kernel image that is already cached on nodes.

kevin: I can manually k8s scale the provisioner job to force more nodes, and mark nodes with cached images as preferred (nodeSelector). Doing that now.

kevin: ```bash
kubectl patch hpa/provisioner -n infra --type='json' -p='[{"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/replicas", "value": 24}]'
# then cordon/taint a few nodes to prefer cached-image nodes
```

jamie: I'll update customer with the mitigation plan and ETA ~15-20m. Also ask them to enable fallback if they're comfortable.

anna: Please add repro steps for engineering so we can root-cause. Customer provided a simple repro: 

anna: ```bash
# reproduce load that uncovers attach lag
wrk -t8 -c60 -d120s http://api.redwood/test-route -H "Authorization: Bearer <tenant-key>"
# watch attach queue: kubectl get svc/provisioning-queue -n infra -o wide
```

maria: For postmortem, we'll need: attach queue lengths, node bootstrap timings, image pull failure counts, provisioner logs, and scheduler events for 01:00-02:00 UTC. I'll add those to the ticket.

kevin: Manual scaling done. I also toggled a soft-fallback policy for t-acme-42 to allow 10% of requests to go to hosted.

deploy-bot: action: toggle-fallback succeeded for tenant=t-acme-42 (by kevin)

jamie: Customer updated — tail latency improving, p99 down to ~1.1s now, some 503s still trickling. They're ok with the fallback while we stabilize. :thumbsup:

anna: Owners/action items: 
- kevin: follow up on node image pull failures (root cause: registry throttling?) — investigate registry metrics and restart backoff logic.
- maria: prepare postmortem artifacts & identify safer prewarm defaults for dedicated pools.
- jamie: communicate final outcome to customer and include rollback plan for the fallback.

maria: One more immediate improvement idea: add an attach admission token TTL so requests don't queue forever — short circuit at 30s and return controlled fallback. Low-risk change we can prototype.

kevin: Noted. I'll also add a short-lived alert rule: if dedicated attach_queue > 80 for > 2m, page SRE and throttle new attaches to prevent cascading image-pull storms.

anna: Thanks all. I'll keep the ticket updated and mark it as being handled.

jamie: I'll keep monitoring metrics for the next 60m. Ping me if we see another bump.

kevin: I'll open an incident doc and drop links once I collect logs.

anna: Closing the slack thread for updates; will repost if anything changes. :white_check_mark:
